_doc: Why a job scored what it scored. The scorer stores a CODE and its arguments - ["title_match", 10] - and this file is the only place the wording lives. It sat as English sentences inside score_job() before, with 'Zurich commute range', 'Switzerland, outside commute range' and 'requires German' baked into shared code: a profile in Lisbon was told about Zurich, and index.html read the CV hits back out by regex-matching the prose. A code survives rewording, translation and a move to another country; a sentence does not. {0} and {1} are the stored arguments, in order. A profile may override any of these under `reason_labels` in its own profile.json.
_legacy: Everything under `legacy` was emitted by the scorer before 2026-09-22, when the goal score was title words + AI words + stack words + geography and the CV fit was five keyword tables read off a CV. Neither is produced any more - both numbers are now 90 points of the posting's own skills plus 10 for a target title - and the codes are kept only so an index written by an older run still reads as sentences instead of as codes.

reasons.goal_skills: {0} - {1} of the {2} skills asked for, weighted by how much you want them (+{3})
reasons.fit_skills: {0} - {1} of the {2} skills asked for, weighted by your experience (+{3})
reasons.title_match: a title you are looking for (+{0})
reasons.fit_none: no description published - fit not assessable

legacy.geo_remote_ok: remote, and can employ you where you live
legacy.geo_country: in your country, outside commuting range
legacy.geo_remote_region: remote in your region, eligibility unconfirmed
legacy.geo_region: in your region, would need relocation
